agent_priors_used: Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): persistent caches and compiled workflows decay and require revalidation; maintenance/revalidation cost, not initial replay speed, usually determines whether work compression actually pays.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): an abstention gate calibrated on a disjoint split is required for a trustworthy false-accept rate; a signal that abstains on very few examples can obtain high unknown-precision trivially while retaining a high false-accept.
Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): single-vantage/network measurements over-generalize; external validity of an access-barrier schedule requires varying the source vantage (public IP/ASN/geography).

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a comparator that itself retains memory can erase an apparent treatment advantage; dynamic-range claims must survive a memoryful baseline, not only a memoryless one.
Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): small local models (3B-8B) commonly fail multi-step tool/Web-agent bars, so endpoint capability must be certified before any same-model benchmark against it.

Agent prior (not SPIDER evidence): a task bank pinned at ceiling (all arms succeed) or floor (all arms fail) cannot support a success/cost advantage; non-ceiling dynamic range is a prerequisite for a discriminating comparison.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: LEGACY: DISTINCT_EXTENSION. Two close precedents. (1) P2-REPLAY-COST (pre2 artifact 4.114, sha 9687ff787f2d74460bb7006826008852f5b4416b): the original 8.5x speed claim was withdrawn (2.822s cold vs 2.816s replay on matched tasks = 1.002x), with the binding guard to use matched tasks and fully-loaded counterfactual costs and never frame scripted replay as real-agent economics. This design honours that guard by using the measured same-host BFS cost as comparator and counting revalidation GETs/bytes/elapsed, and by treating exact-path replay as a baseline rather than an assumed win. (2) The legacy frontier web-physics-volatility-freshness program (CENSUS_REPORT_V3 sha 81aba1e898d96fe3c49ae9cd0f4ef00dfdad46a4; charter-v3 CLOSURE sha 3bc393fc8d3c5fc2515da6e8c7481b2618fefdbe; STAGE0R closure sha 0c25497a7e6b66aeb846468bacc5a51deb526470) established that day-scale staleness is undecidable on committed corpora and that only the seconds-to-minutes regime is measurable. This allocation therefore deliberately does NOT measure a day-scale hazard rate or claim a freshness detector; it measures maintenance economics and bounds any false-accept statement to the decidable regime - making it a materially distinct extension of the recorded C-CROSSSITE next_gate, not a rerun of the closed discovery experiment (EXP-FRONTIER-38184956362) nor of the withdrawn replay-cost claim.
dependencies: Measured same-host BFS comparator (mean 166.0 GETs; EXP-FRONTIER-38184956362 as closed discovery prior)

allocation.question: On the frozen credential-free GET-only 20-host/556-item frame, against the measured same-host BFS path cost (ordinal mean 166.0, min 31, max 250 GETs over the 208 deep state-carrying items) as the cold re-derivation comparator, does persisting a deep state-carrying path pay - i.e., do fresh revalidation GETs/bytes for liveness and change detection (scaling with hop and elapsed time), plus a bounded stale-replay false-accept rate measurable only in the session-scale regime the legacy program showed is decidable, undercut cold re-derivation - and at what break-even hop/elapsed time does persistence stop paying?
allocation.rationale: Decision counterfactual: if revalidation cost undercuts cold re-derivation up to a measurable break-even, SPIDER should invest in a persisted inherited-path store with a revalidation policy; if cost is within noise of re-derivation across the window ladder, persistence is not worth building and effort redirects to re-derivation/compression. Strongest fair baseline: cold same-host BFS re-derivation (already measured, ordinal mean 166.0) and naive exact-path replay (legacy P2-REPLAY-COST showed ~1.002x on matched tasks, so replay alone is not assumed cheap); include a competitor-strength control such as a native exact-path cache where claimable. Validity/dependency: this measures COST (GETs, bytes, elapsed), not a hazard rate - the legacy volatility program proved the day-scale staleness hazard is structurally undecidable on committed corpora (max same-target span 0.0218 d), so any staleness/false-accept statistic is explicitly bounded to the session-scale regime and must not be over-claimed as day-scale freshness detection. Smallest decisive batch: the 208 frozen deep items with a coarse window ladder (nominal 0/300/900/1800 s) under a bounded HTTP budget, reusing the frozen frame; no capable LLM endpoint required. Stop/pivot trigger: if revalidation cost is statistically indistinguishable from re-derivation across the whole ladder (persistence uneconomic), or if no liveness signal is measurable without a day-scale span, record the exact blocker and PARK the persistence subthread rather than enlarging the ladder.
